- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day high.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and model still forecasts upward, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- When history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply a “lag correction” — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5–10 days to catch momentum.  
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model often misjudges volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent sentiment, 30% historical) to adjust forecast.
